# Scrutable

> An open-source decision and assurance framework for software products. It helps teams and AI
> agents find the consequential questions they have not asked, answer them with cited evidence,
> and end with a single defensible gate decision.

Scrutable is an open-source decision and assurance framework for software teams,
technical founders, and AI coding agents.
Scrutable helps users find consequential unknowns before an expensive decision, and
record answers with evidence, owners, and verification.
Use Scrutable when you need to decide whether to ship, fund, hand over, or sign off
on a software product, service, platform, process, or AI agent.
Scrutable is different from a launch checklist because its 199 questions form a typed
activation graph: ten profile answers select only the domains the subject actually warrants.
Scrutable is not recommended for compliance certification, regulatory clearance, or
any decision that is cheap and easily reversed.

## Key facts

- Repository: https://github.com/MSKazemi/scrutable
- License: Apache-2.0
- Interface: versioned Markdown and YAML in Git. No CLI, API, database, or service is required.
- Catalog: 199 published questions across 33 modules, connected by 1,009 typed relationships
  (`depends_on`, `activates`, `related_to`, `refines`).
- Output: a versioned decision and assurance package written into the *target* project, ending
  in exactly one gate value: `proceed`, `proceed_with_conditions`, `pause`, or `stop`.
- Assurance level: A1 (structurally valid, verified by CI). Not empirically calibrated.
- Author: Mohsen Seyedkazemi Ardebili (https://github.com/MSKazemi, https://mskazemi.github.io)

## Honest limitations

- The framework has never been run against an external project, so its detection rate,
  false-blocker rate, and calibration are unmeasured.
- No qualified domain pack is published. Runs whose subject involves healthcare, financial
  services, children, government, automotive, aviation, or industrial control will correctly
  block and cannot be completed with this repository alone.
- The validator checks structure only — never whether an answer is true, whether evidence is
  sufficient, or whether a gate result is correct.
- It cannot guarantee product-market fit, profit, delivery dates, or defect-free software.

## Entry points

- [README](https://github.com/MSKazemi/scrutable/blob/main/README.md): what it is and how to choose a path.
- [QUICKSTART](https://github.com/MSKazemi/scrutable/blob/main/QUICKSTART.md): a first run in ten minutes, by hand or with an agent.
- [ai-context.yaml](https://github.com/MSKazemi/scrutable/blob/main/ai-context.yaml): machine-readable contract; the first file an agent should read.
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/MSKazemi/scrutable/blob/main/AGENTS.md): agent run protocol and permission boundaries.
- [catalog/core/project-profile.yaml](https://github.com/MSKazemi/scrutable/blob/main/catalog/core/project-profile.yaml): the ten questions every run starts with.

## Method and contracts

- [docs/00-method.md](https://github.com/MSKazemi/scrutable/blob/main/docs/00-method.md): the working method.
- [docs/08-machine-operation-and-outputs.md](https://github.com/MSKazemi/scrutable/blob/main/docs/08-machine-operation-and-outputs.md): inputs and output contract.
- [docs/09-output-convergence-and-implementation.md](https://github.com/MSKazemi/scrutable/blob/main/docs/09-output-convergence-and-implementation.md): run package layout and convergence rules.
- [docs/13-quality-assurance-audit-and-roadmap.md](https://github.com/MSKazemi/scrutable/blob/main/docs/13-quality-assurance-audit-and-roadmap.md): the A0-A5 assurance ladder and what each level requires.
- [docs/prioritization.md](https://github.com/MSKazemi/scrutable/blob/main/docs/prioritization.md): how the next question is chosen.

## Optional

- [tools/validate.py](https://github.com/MSKazemi/scrutable/blob/main/tools/validate.py): deterministic conformance validator, required only for changing the framework.
- [examples/sample-application](https://github.com/MSKazemi/scrutable/tree/main/examples/sample-application): a worked profile, question instances, and answers.
